summary.one_liner: A small Python library for building LLM-controlled agents that loop through Thought, Action and Observation steps, inspired by langchain but kept minimal.
summary.what_it_does: The library provides an Agent class that is driven by a language model and a set of tools. The agent is instructed by a prompt describing how to solve tasks with tools, then runs a loop of Thought, Action, Observation until it has enough information to give a final answer. Thoughts and actions (with action input) are generated by the LLM, while observations come from running a tool, such as Python REPL output or Google search results. The README names three built-in tools: a Python REPL, SerpAPI-based Google search, and Hacker News search. Users can also write custom tools or omit tools entirely. The README states the code is meant to be readable in very few lines, to help people understand how agents work.
use_cases: learn how LLM agents work internally
build a simple tool-using agent in Python
let an LLM run Python code to answer questions
search Google through an LLM agent
search Hacker News with an agent
prototype custom tools for an LLM
how_to_run: export SERPAPI_API_KEY='your-key' (only if using Google search)
notable: Deliberately minimal: built from scratch to show the core parts of an agent without langchain's extra abstraction layers
Thought/Action/Observation loop where the LLM output drives tool calls and tool output is appended to the prompt
Built-in tools for Python REPL execution, Google search via SerpAPI, and Hacker News search
Tools are plain components, so custom tools can be added or tools omitted
caveats: Requires an OpenAI API key; the Google search tool additionally requires a SerpAPI key
README does not state a license
README is brief and does not describe supported models beyond OpenAI
keywords: answer questions with llm and search
